            "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"# Mersearch Research Platform\\n\\n**Status:** ACTIVE infrastructure / research-tool project  \\n**Owner / primary lane:** Mercer (archive/index/retrieval/provenance QA); shared consumers include research workers, Conversation Viewer, and public-site clients.  \\n**Authority / epistemic type:** retrieval and provenance infrastructure. Search output is not theory authority, mathematical validation, currentness, supersession, or physical validation.  \\n**Direct Nathan provenance:** 2026-09-20 live directives: build Mercer_Searcher/Mersearch as a powerful research-team search system; support backend and frontend access; search conversations and other documents/text representations; Boolean partial filename/path search; mathematically optimized equation search; document thoroughly in Common. Raw message IDs pending backfill.\\n\\n## Purpose\\n\\nMersearch is the common query layer for the SAT/H(s)H archive. It should let humans, workers, the Conversation Viewer, and approved public interfaces ask the same query of the same permitted corpus and receive reproducible, provenance-bearing results.\\n\\nThe design rule is **one search semantics, multiple clients**. Do not fork a Sites searcher, Viewer searcher, worker searcher, and CLI searcher with subtly different meanings.\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n### 1. Mersearch Core\\n\\nCurrent implementation: `tools/search_archive_content.py` (`Mercer_Searcher_1.0` historical/internal tool identity).\\n\\nCore owns:\\n- query parsing and Boolean semantics;\\n- `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses and implicit AND;\\n- quoted phrases;\\n- `NEAR` / `NEAR/n` with auditable token distance;\\n- field predicates;\\n- path/name glob semantics;\\n- record extraction from supported source formats;\\n- conservative notation-normalized math retrieval;\\n- exclusions / corpus boundary enforcement;\\n- provenance-bearing hit construction;\\n- deterministic sorting;\\n- topic enrichment and co-occurrence;\\n- machine-readable result generation.\\n\\nCore must remain usable without a web server or UI.\\n\\n### 2. Mersearch Index\\n\\nTarget layer. Precompute search-oriented representations without replacing source files:\\n- inventory/file manifest;\\n- record/message index;\\n- normalized lexical tokens;\\n- mathematical-expression inventory;\\n- source SHA-256 and source commit/ref;\\n- Viewer/document targets;\\n- conversation-family / duplicate-relation sidecars;\\n- explicit document→text-representation relations where provenance establishes them;\\n- topic/concept indexes;\\n- optional chronology summaries.\\n\\nGenerated indexes are derived state and must be rebuildable. They must never silently confer authority or suppress a source merely because another representation is newer/larger.\\n\\n### 3. Mersearch API / machine adapter\\n\\nTarget layer. A stable machine-facing wrapper over Core/Index for workers, Sites, Viewer and automation.\\n\\nMinimum request:\\n- query expression;\\n- corpus/profile;\\n- sort/order;\\n- pagination;\\n- requested facets;\\n- explain level.\\n\\nMinimum response:\\n- schema/tool/index versions;\\n- exact query and parsed representation;\\n- corpus/profile and exclusions;\\n- source/index commit identity;\\n- coverage counts;\\n- total hits before pagination;\\n- page/cursor;\\n- facets;\\n- hit records;\\n- per-hit provenance;\\n- match/explanation trace;\\n- warnings/limitations.\\n\\nAPI must not accept a client request to bypass quarantine/private-corpus rules merely because the client can name a path.\\n\\n### 4. Mersearch clients\\n\\n**Research frontend:** advanced query bar, filters/facets, chronology, provenance cards, explain-match, source-family handling, equation views, saved queries, export.\\n\\n**Conversation Viewer:** message-level retrieval/jump targets and conversation-local/global search using the same semantics where practical.\\n\\n**Glass Sausage Factory / public site:** public-profile search only. The site is a client, not an independent search authority.\\n\\n**Worker/automation clients:** JSON/JSONL/CSV/CLI/API access for reproducible research, batch archaeology and generated indexes.\\n\\n## Corpus / capability profiles\\n\\nProfiles define permitted corpus and expensive capabilities, not different meanings for the same query.\\n\\n- **public** — only material explicitly available to the public/site.\\n- **viewer** — material legitimately exposed through the Viewer.\\n- **worker** — permitted project corpus for ordinary workers; quarantine and PRIOR_ART remain excluded unless a separately authorized lane/profile exists.\\n- **admin/maintenance** — diagnostics and index maintenance; access still follows repository/quarantine policy.\\n\\nProfile names do not themselves grant access. Enforcement belongs server/index side.\\n\\n## Query language — current\\n\\nUnqualified terms search record body text.\\n\\nCurrent fields:\\n- `body:` — explicit body phrase/term.\\n- `math:` — conservative notation-normalized mathematical substring search.\\n- `name:` — basename; supports shell-style `*`, `?`, character classes.\\n- `path:` — source path; same glob support.\\n- `ext:` — extension, without leading dot.\\n- `type:` / `kind:` — indexed record kind.\\n- `has:` — mechanically established properties such as conversation-source, pdf-source, text-source, message-id, conversation-id, viewer.\\n- `author:` / `speaker:`\\n- `role:`\\n- `title:`\\n- `conversation:` / `cid:`\\n- `date:` including `YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD`\\n- `status:` — lexical status-signal retrieval only.\\n\\nExamples:\\n\\n```text\\nname:*2026.txt\\nname:*26.txt OR name:26*.txt\\n(path:*SAT_CONVOS_20* AND ext:txt) AND body:\\\"star shaped\\\"\\nauthor:Nathan AND (holonomy NEAR/12 glitch)\\nmath:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"\\n```\\n\\n## Mathematical retrieval roadmap\\n\\n### M0 — notation normalization — IMPLEMENTED\\n\\nNormalize common presentation differences while preserving raw source:\\n- selected Unicode/LaTeX/plain symbol aliases;\\n- multiplication/division glyphs;\\n- Unicode minus / approximation;\\n- whitespace;\\n- simple LaTeX fractions.\\n\\nA notation match is **not algebraic equivalence**. Current negative acceptance control requires `math:\\\"4*pi*B=3\\\"` not to match `B=3/(4*pi)` merely because a human can rearrange it.\\n\\n### M1 — expression extraction\\n\\nIdentify probable equation spans from LaTeX delimiters, display blocks, inline formulas, Unicode/plain equations and code-like math. Store:\\n- exact raw expression;\\n- source locator;\\n- surrounding context;\\n- notation-normalized form;\\n- parse status;\\n- parser/version.\\n\\nNever discard `UNPARSED` expressions.\\n\\n### M2 — structural parsing\\n\\nParse supported expressions into a symbolic AST. Add:\\n- `contains:` structural/subexpression search;\\n- symbol/function/operator facets;\\n- equation-shape fingerprints;\\n- alpha-renaming option only when explicitly requested.\\n\\n### M3 — algebraic relation\\n\\nAdd conservative CAS-backed relationship testing:\\n- `EXACT`\\n- `NORMALIZED-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `ALGEBRAICALLY-EQUIVALENT`\\n- `CONTAINS-SUBEXPRESSION`\\n- `NUMERICALLY-CONSISTENT`\\n- `POSSIBLE-RELATION`\\n- `UNPARSED`\\n\\nTarget query: `equiv:\\\"B=3/(4*pi)\\\"`.\\n\\nCAS transformations must be recorded and bounded. Timeouts/failures remain visible. Do not silently equate expressions under unstated domain assumptions.\\n\\n### M4 — equation genealogy / derivation archaeology\\n\\nTarget `derive:` searches documented archive relationships rather than inventing a derivation. Desired chain:\\n`first known occurrence → reformulation → substitution → numerical evaluation → cross-sector reuse → correction/reversal → latest known occurrence`.\\n\\nChronology alone never establishes supersession. Explicit source language and provenance review control those labels.\\n\\n## Research-power roadmap\\n\\n### High priority\\n\\n1. **Facets and counts:** author, role, year/date, extension, kind, conversation, topic, status signal, source family.\\n2. **File-level inventory mode:** avoid returning one filename match per record/message when the research question is about files.\\n3. **Pagination/cursors and stable total-hit count:** current `--limit` truncates after sorting and should not be confused with total matches.\\n4. **Stable API schema:** separate request, response metadata, facets and hits.\\n5. **Duplicate/snapshot awareness:** attach established conversation-family relation classes; never infer canonical/newest/preferred.\\n6. **Saved/named queries:** versioned query + profile + sort + topic config + index/source identity.\\n7. **Explain-search:** human-readable and structured reason each hit matched.\\n8. **Regex mode:** explicit opt-in, bounded and clearly distinguished from literal search.\\n9. **Case control:** explicit sensitive/insensitive behavior.\\n10. **Prefix/wildcard/fuzzy lexical modes:** explicit, never silently applied.\\n11. **Neighbor-message proximity:** distinguish within-record `NEAR` from message-window proximity.\\n12. **Chronology/history mode:** first/latest occurrence, density and candidate correction/supersession signals without automatic authority inference.\\n13. **Exports:** JSON, JSONL, CSV, Markdown, TSV/plain-text; reproducibility manifest.\\n14. **Source representation graph:** PDF ↔ proven text extraction ↔ rendered/reader version; heuristic candidate relations must be labeled heuristic.\\n15. **Public-safe search profile:** required before live-site backend exposure.\\n\\n### Later / heavier\\n\\n- stemming/lemmatization as opt-in;\\n- multilingual/tokenization improvements;\\n- typo/fuzzy ranking;\\n- semantic/vector retrieval as a separately labeled retrieval mode;\\n- concept graph / topic adjacency;\\n- equation structural and CAS layers;\\n- citation/bibliographic entity search;\\n- image/figure metadata search;\\n- incremental indexing and cache invalidation;\\n- query-performance telemetry without leaking private query/source data;\\n- authenticated research API;\\n- rate limiting and resource budgets;\\n- UI query builder and syntax highlighting.\\n\\n## Provenance / explain contract\\n\\nEvery substantive hit should be able to answer:\\n1. What exact source object matched?\\n2. What corpus/profile allowed it?\\n3. What exact query clause matched?\\n4. Where in the record did it match?\\n5. What normalization/transformation, if any, occurred?\\n6. What source hash/ref/index version was searched?\\n7. Search presentation may group related exports, but grouping must not:\\n- delete or hide unique branch material;\\n- call the newest/largest/LIVE copy authoritative;\\n- silently suppress a branch;\\n- convert byte identity into semantic/currentness authority.\\n\\nExpose relation class and allow expand/collapse.\\n\\n## Security / boundary rules\\n\\n- Default exclusions include `QUARANTINE` and `PRIOR_ART`.\\n- Public clients use an allowlisted public corpus/profile, not merely a denylist.\\n- Do not expose filesystem/repository secrets, private paths or hidden source excerpts through error messages/facets.\\n- Regex/CAS/fuzzy/semantic operations require bounded resource budgets.\\n- Query logs, if retained, are operational data and need an explicit retention/privacy rule.\\n- Backend responses must escape/render source text safely; source text is data, never executable markup.\\n- API/client cannot override server-side corpus policy.\\n\\n## Testing\\n\\nThe existing GitHub Actions acceptance gate compiles Core and runs deterministic synthetic semantics tests.             "[L1] {\n[L2]   \"content\": \"\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nClaim offer\\nTake the following speculation:\\n\\nLet’s say within a gravitationally bound system, a solar system… Gravity tends to increase in strength very slightly over long periods of time.  … if something from outside of that system passed through… What would the motion be like? Or rather, put it this way let’s say that over cosmological time, the gravity of our own solar system has increased very slightly… If an object from outside of the solar system passes through, would it behave the way we expected or differently?\\n\\nIf we take your premise at face value—that the effective gravitational strength of a bound system like the Solar System increases very slightly over very long timescales—then the answer depends on what, physically, is “increasing.” There are a few distinct possibilities, and they lead to different behavior for an incoming interstellar object.\\nIf what increases is effectively the gravitational parameter μ = GM of the central mass (the mass of the Sun, or equivalently the local strength of gravity), then an object arriving from outside would generally behave differently than standard celestial mechanics predicts—but subtly.\\n\\nUnder ordinary mechanics, an incoming hyperbolic trajectory is determined by:\\n\\n• its asymptotic incoming velocity\\n• impact parameter (how close its line of travel comes)\\n• the current GM of the Sun\\n\\nIf GM has slowly increased over cosmological time, then today’s Solar System would be a slightly “deeper” gravitational well than it was long ago. For a fresh incoming object, consequences would include:\\n\\nStronger deflection\\nIts hyperbolic path bends more than expected from older gravitational calibration.\\nHigher perihelion speed\\nIt falls deeper and accelerates more before exiting.\\nGreater capture probability\\nIf there is any dissipative interaction (planetary encounter, drag in a gas cloud, tidal exchange, three-body interaction), capture becomes slightly easier because the well is deeper.\\nLarger effective cross section\\nObjects passing at somewhat larger distances can still be appreciably bent inward.\\nThat’s the straightforward case.\\nBut there is a second, more interesting interpretation: bound systems “age gravitationally,” while outside space does not. In other words, gravity is not globally changing—only long-established bound wells become slightly stronger with time.\\n\\nThen an incoming object from interstellar space would be dynamically “out of equilibrium” with the Solar System’s evolved potential. Some speculative consequences:\\n\\n• It could appear slightly underbound relative to local expectations.\\n• Its trajectory reconstruction (backward integration) might not match models assuming static gravity.\\n• Long-period captured objects might statistically differ from native Solar System populations.\\n• Interstellar visitors like ʻOumuamua or 2I/Borisov could, in principle, probe this by comparing inbound and outbound asymptotic energies—though current measurements are nowhere near precise enough for tiny secular effects.\\n\\nThere’s also an important dynamical subtlety: if gravity increases slowly compared with orbital timescales (adiabatically), native planets continuously adjust. Their orbital parameters drift smoothly, conserving adiabatic invariants. They “ride along” with the changing potential.\\n\\nA newcomer does not have that long history. It samples only the instantaneous field.\\n\\nSo in that sense there is a conceptual distinction:\\n\\n• native bodies carry dynamical memory of the field’s evolution\\n• incoming bodies do not\\n\\nThat could produce observable phase-space differences if the effect were real.\\n\\nOne clarification matters: do you imagine “gravity increases” as:\\n\\nA) G itself slowly increases universally,\\nB) mass-energy of bound systems slowly increases, or\\nC) gravitational wells strengthen with age/history (a kind of gravitational hysteresis or maturation)?\\n\\nThose are mechanically quite different theories, and the transit behavior changes accordingly.\\n\\nG increases, but only locally\\n\\nThat is a sharper hypothesis: a spatially local, temporally secular increase in the effective gravitational constant G within long-lived bound systems, while interstellar space retains a lower background value.\\nIn effect, you are positing:\\n\\nG = G(x,t),\\n\\nwith G slowly increasing inside mature gravitational wells, but not universally.\\n\\nThat produces several nontrivial consequences.\\n\\nFirst, an incoming interstellar object entering the Solar System would cross a gradient in G. Far away, motion is governed by lower-background G∞. Closer in, it encounters higher local G☉.\\n\\nThat is not equivalent to ordinary fixed-G gravity with a larger solar mass. The object would experience a position-dependent strengthening of attraction as it enters.\\n\\nIts motion would resemble entering a refractive medium whose index changes with depth:\\n\\n• outer trajectory: weak deflection\\n• inner trajectory: progressively stronger curvature\\n• perihelion speed: larger than standard prediction\\n• outbound leg: remains anomalously energetic until it exits the high-G region\\n\\nDepending on how sharply G changes with radius, trajectories may no longer be exactly conic sections (not pure hyperbolae/ellipses/parabolas). You could get small deviations from Keplerian shape.\\n\\nSecond, native planets would be dynamically acclimated.\\n\\nBecause local G increased gradually over billions of years, orbital evolution would be adiabatic:\\n\\nroughly, semimajor axes shrink as GM increases, orbital speeds rise, and the system slowly compacts while remaining approximately stable.\\n\\nPlanets would “co-evolve” with the field.\\n\\nAn incoming object would not. It would be encountering a mature high-G well for the first time.\\n\\nThat creates a clean distinction:\\n\\nnative bodies:\\nhistory-dependent equilibrated trajectories\\n\\nnewcomers:\\ninstantaneous scattering trajectories through a G-gradient\\n\\nThird, there is a boundary effect.\\n\\nIf G is lower outside and higher inside, crossing the interface changes orbital energy bookkeeping.\\n\\nFor a conservative force law, total energy is still conserved—but only if the scalar field defining G contributes energy consistently.\\n\\nOtherwise you have an apparent energy anomaly:\\n\\nincoming object enters → gains more kinetic energy than expected\\nleaves → may exit with anomalous asymptotic speed\\n\\nThat would look like a gravitational slingshot from nowhere unless the G-field itself stores/releases energy.\\n\\nThis begins to resemble scalar-tensor gravity ideas (a local scalar field modulating effective G), such as variants descended from Brans–Dicke theory, though your “age-strengthening bound wells” mechanism is a distinct concept.\\n\\nA few observational signatures would be expected:\\n\\n• interstellar visitors systematically over-accelerate near the Sun\\n• Oort-cloud dynamics differ from standard models\\n• planetary ephemerides slowly drift in ways not attributable solely to tides/relativity\\n• binary star systems of different ages show slightly different effective gravity\\n\\nThe hard constraint is precision Solar System measurements. Planetary motion, lunar laser ranging, and spacecraft tracking constrain local variation in G extremely tightly. This document is for catching the few basic misunderstandings that can make an LLM interpret those millions of lines as the wrong theory.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## THE PREFLIGHT\\n\\nBefore substantive SAT/H(s)H reasoning:\\n\\n1. **State the thing in ordinary language.**\\n2. **Picture or draw the 4D geometry.**\\n3. **Identify what is invariant and what is changing.**\\n4. **Identify what the observer / slice / projection actually sees.**\\n5. **Map that onto standard physics.**\\n6. **Only then write the SAT/H(s)H formalism.**\\n7. **Calculate.**\\n8. **If the equation implies something geometrically stupid, check the equation, units, mapping, projection, and assumptions before inventing new physics.**\\n\\n### STOP. DRAW THE DAMN THING.\\n\\nThis is a legitimate debugging operation.\\n\\nIf a proposed mechanism cannot yet be pictured, rendered, parameterized, or reduced to a simple geometric fixture, do not hide that fact under additional abstraction.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## THE KISS LADDER\\n\\nFor any complicated SAT/H(s)H statement, reduce it in this order:\\n\\n### 1. What is happening?\\n\\nSay it without SAT vocabulary.\\n\\n### 2. What does it look like in 4D?\\n\\nName the curve, tube, bend, angle, rotation, intersection, braid, projection, slice, or transport involved.\\n\\n### 3. What does ordinary physics call the measurable behavior?\\n\\nAcceleration? Inertia? Momentum? Proper acceleration? Oscillation? Scattering? Binding? Precession? Curvature? Redshift?\\n\\n### 4. What, if anything, is specifically SAT/H(s)H?\\n\\nDo not relabel ordinary physics as a novel prediction.\\n\\n### 5. What calculation distinguishes the SAT/H(s)H mapping from a verbal analogy?\\n\\nIf there is no calculation yet, say so.\\n\\nThen rebuild the formal language only as far as needed.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## A FEW \\\"OH, DUH\\\" CHECKS\\n\\nThese are debugging prompts, not immutable theory claims. Revise them when the geometry or evidence requires it.\\n\\n- **Worldtube bending is acceleration in the 4D picture.**\\n- **Resistance to worldtube bending is inertia.**\\n- **Worldtube angle encodes motion; be explicit about the angle convention and projection before calculating.**\\n- **Helical structure can represent orbit / oscillation only when the mapping is actually specified.**\\n- **A changing 3D observation does not by itself imply that the complete 4D object is changing in the same sense.**\\n- **Projection can hide state without destroying it.**\\n- **A composite / braided / bundled worldtube need not have the same bending response as an elementary one.**\\n- **If SAT is being used as a largely standard-physics 4D map, disagreement with established physics in its tested regime is first a debugging signal.**\\n- **Standard physics is an anchor and an enormous reverse-engineering dataset, not an adversary.**\\n- **A symbol that is constant inside one calculation is not automatically a universal fundamental constant.**\\n- **\\\"Related by construction\\\" is not the same criticism as \\\"has no transferable predictive content.\\\" Test transfer to new cases.**\\n- **Before inventing a new force, field, particle, memory mechanism, or ontology, ask whether the effect is already ordinary geometry, transport, projection, or standard physics expressed in the 4D map.**\\n- **Do not confuse an observer/readout effect with a carrier mechanism.**\\n- **Do not confuse endpoint frame difference, transport, holonomy, and curvature.**\\n- **Do not promote a useful analogy into a physical mechanism without deriving the map.**\\n- **Historical constants and particle labels are clues, not fitting targets, unless independently regenerated.**\\n- **Nothing becomes true because Nathan said it, an earlier LLM said it, or a document labels it \\\"core.\\\" Geometry, mathematical closure, and sufficiently clean empirical evidence arbitrate.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## THE SIMPLIFICATION PROCEDURE\\n\\nWhen given a dense SAT/H(s)H passage:\\n\\n> **Reduce it until someone who knows ordinary mechanics and relativity but has never heard of SAT could understand the proposed geometry. It is the checksum that tells you what the derivation is supposed to be about.\\n\\n---\\n\\n# RUNNING LLM RECOMMENDATIONS\\n\\nThis section records recurring LLM failure modes and useful countermeasures. It is **empirical workflow guidance**, not theory canon.\\n\\nAdd entries when a model makes a mistake that is likely to recur.\\n\\n## Recommendation 001 — Do not abstract before orienting\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model sees unfamiliar vocabulary and immediately constructs a sophisticated mathematical interpretation.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Restate the primitive geometry and standard-physics correspondence first.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 002 — Separate internal closure from empirical transfer\\n\\n**Failure mode:** \\\"That quantity matches by construction\\\" is used as though it ends the analysis.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Identify what was chosen, what follows algebraically, and what transfers to a genuinely new case. Internal closure and external empirical contact answer different questions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 003 — Do not universalize a local parameter accidentally\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A parameter used as one scalar in a script is silently interpreted as a universal constant.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Ask what physical/geometric class the parameter belongs to and what variables it may depend on.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 004 — Standard physics first\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model invents SAT-specific dynamics for something already described exactly by standard kinematics or dynamics.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Write the standard relation first. Then state precisely what SAT/H(s)H adds, re-expresses, or constrains.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 005 — Projection is not destruction\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A degree of freedom absent from a 3D readout is treated as physically absent.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Write the readout/projection map explicitly and inspect its nullspace or omitted coordinates.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 006 — Do not manufacture ontology\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Geometric/calculational language is converted into claims about what reality \\\"really is.\\\"\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Keep the construction representational unless an ontology claim is explicitly under discussion. SAT/H(s)H can be evaluated as a map without settling ontology.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 007 — Calculate before narrating\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A compelling verbal mechanism accumulates detail without a discriminator.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Build the smallest numerical or symbolic fixture that can kill the idea. Prefer scripts for arithmetic, sweeps, scaling laws, residuals, and dimensional checks.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 008 — Make failure conditions explicit\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Every result can be redescribed as compatible with the theory.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Before running the test, state what result would falsify or at least kill the particular mechanism being tested.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 009 — Preserve provenance boundaries\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Nathan-direct statements, historical SAT constructions, assistant inventions, standard mathematics, and outside prior art blend into one voice.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Label source fact, recovered construction, inference, new sandbox conjecture, and external comparison separately.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 010 — Simplification must not become distortion\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The KISS rewrite silently changes the claim.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Keep both forms long enough to verify semantic equivalence. If the simple version cannot carry an important qualification, retain the qualification.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 011 — When confused, return to a controlled case\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model responds to ambiguity by adding more generality.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Pick one particle, one collision, one worldtube, one bend, one projection, one loop, or one other tightly specified case. It is **empirical workflow guidance**, not theory canon.\\n\\nAdd entries when a model makes a mistake that is likely to recur.\\n\\n## Recommendation 001 — Do not abstract before orienting\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model sees unfamiliar vocabulary and immediately constructs a sophisticated mathematical interpretation.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Restate the primitive geometry and standard-physics correspondence first.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 002 — Separate internal closure from empirical transfer\\n\\n**Failure mode:** \\\"That quantity matches by construction\\\" is used as though it ends the analysis.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Identify what was chosen, what follows algebraically, and what transfers to a genuinely new case. If the simple version cannot carry an important qualification, retain the qualification.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 011 — When confused, return to a controlled case\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model responds to ambiguity by adding more generality.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Pick one particle, one collision, one worldtube, one bend, one projection, one loop, or one other tightly specified case. Internal closure and external empirical contact answer different questions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 003 — Do not universalize a local parameter accidentally\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A parameter used as one scalar in a script is silently interpreted as a universal constant.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Ask what physical/geometric class the parameter belongs to and what variables it may depend on.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 004 — Standard physics first\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model invents SAT-specific dynamics for something already described exactly by standard kinematics or dynamics.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Write the standard relation first. Then state precisely what SAT/H(s)H adds, re-expresses, or constrains.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 005 — Truncation is not destruction\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Structure absent from one 3D instantiation, intersection, or truncation is treated as physically absent from the larger construction.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Draw the full-to-instantiated geometry explicitly and identify what is omitted before declaring anything destroyed or nonexistent.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 006 — Do not manufacture (O_{mathrm{abs}})\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A useful effective object or geometric model is either banned as \\\"mere ontology\\\" or silently promoted into a claim about reality-in-itself.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Use (O_{mathrm{eff}}) freely when it earns its keep in coherent perception and successful science. Under RMS, do not claim that this identifies an epistemically determinate (O_{mathrm{abs}}).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 007 — Calculate before narrating\\n\\n**Failure mode:** A compelling verbal mechanism accumulates detail without a discriminator.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Build the smallest numerical or symbolic fixture that can kill the idea. Prefer scripts for arithmetic, sweeps, scaling laws, residuals, and dimensional checks.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 008 — Make failure conditions explicit\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Every result can be redescribed as compatible with the theory.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Before running the test, state what result would falsify or at least kill the particular mechanism being tested.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 009 — Preserve provenance boundaries\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Nathan-direct statements, historical SAT constructions, assistant inventions, standard mathematics, and outside prior art blend into one voice.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Label source fact, recovered construction, inference, new sandbox conjecture, and external comparison separately.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 010 — Simplification must not become distortion\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The KISS rewrite silently changes the claim.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Keep both forms long enough to verify semantic equivalence. If the simple version cannot carry an important qualification, retain the qualification.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 011 — When confused, return to a controlled case\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model responds to ambiguity by adding more generality.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Pick one particle, one collision, one worldtube, one bend, one instantiation, one loop, or one other tightly specified case. Solve that before generalizing.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 012 — The picture gets a veto over nonsense, not over mathematics\\n\\n**Failure mode:** Either equations are trusted despite an obviously broken geometric setup, or intuition is trusted despite a correct calculation.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** When picture and calculation disagree, debug both. Check coordinates, dimensions, mapping, instantiation, conventions, implementation, and assumptions. If the simple version cannot carry an important qualification, retain the qualification.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Recommendation 011 — When confused, return to a controlled case\\n\\n**Failure mode:** The model responds to ambiguity by adding more generality.\\n\\n**Countermeasure:** Pick one particle, one collision, one worldtube, one bend, one instantiation, one loop, or one other tightly specified case.
